text:
oliver: Hi, new hire here. VPN (Okta AnyConnect split-tunnel) connects but I can't reach our internal Postgres at db.internal.redwood.dev:5432. Psql from my Mac times out, but colleagues on corp wifi can reach it. Any quick debugging tips?
sophie: welcome! first quick checks: can you ping the DB IP? and does `dig db.internal.redwood.dev` return an internal 10.40.x.x address on your machine?
oliver: ping fails. `dig` returns public IP. On Windows laptop VPN dns shows internal IP. I'm on a home ISP with AnyConnect.
mike: sounds like DNS + split-tunnel on macOS. Often the system resolver or a browser proxy is taking precedence. Try `scutil --dns` to see the order. Also `dscacheutil -flushcache` after VPN connects.
oliver: `scutil --dns` shows VPN DNS but lookup still resolves to public due to cached results. Flushing cache didn't help.
sophie: other option: tunnel the DB connection through the bastion via SSH local port forwarding. Example:
```
ssh -L 5433:db.internal.redwood.dev:5432 ec2-bastion
# then psql -h localhost -p 5433 -U you dbname
```
That avoids relying on OS-level DNS/routing.
oliver: that's a good workaround. Is there a way to make all apps use the VPN DNS?
mike: For macOS, some apps use system proxy settings or mDNS. If it's critical, infra can push a config for managed machines to prefer VPN DNS and add no-proxy exceptions. Otherwise, you can add a host entry to `/etc/hosts` for the short term: `sudo echo "10.40.9.12 db.internal.redwood.dev" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts` (just a temp fix).
oliver: I tried the ssh tunnel and it worked. Thanks. Quick Q: is adding to /etc/hosts OK security-wise?
sophie: fine for short-term debugging but avoid committing or sharing that file. If you need persistent resolution, open an infra ticket so they can set managed DNS or fix split-tunnel propagation for your region.
infra-bot: Docs: https://wiki.redwood.internal/vpn/split-tunnel-db-access  includes bastion examples, host file note, and ticket template.
oliver: will open a ticket and use the SSH tunnel for now. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
